source.title: Samples, Sources, Space: Decomposing Data Scale in Spatially Structured Representation Learning of Human Brain Microarchitecture
source.authors: Christian Schiffer; Mathis Bode; T. Lippert; K. Amunts; Timo Dickscheid

page_placements.theme: Data diversity and coverage are distinct from sample volume

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests downstream performance scaling in a different setting and with a different measure from the original language-model loss studies: image encoders are assessed using linear-probe macro-F1.
record.gate_note: The paper cites language-model scaling laws but does not measure held-out language-model cross-entropy, fit power laws to pretraining loss, or test loss extrapolation. The relevant results are downstream macro-F1 measurements across data, compute, and model-capacity settings.
record.test_reason: The study trains 93 image ViTs (ViT-B/L/H, contrastive SpatialNCE pretraining on brain histology). It varies unique samples, optimization steps and model size, and measures downstream linear-probe macro-F1. It is a new setting (non-text, non-LM) with results on whether downstream performance improves with scale (V6). It fits no power law to held-out pretraining loss, so V1–V5 and V7 are not tested. The logit-linear-in-log2 form is assumed in the mixed model, not tested or extrapolated.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors also conclude that broader spatial coverage improves representations. They add that inter-subject variation strongly affects generalization, yet adding subjects at a fixed budget brings no benefit. They frame sample count, source diversity and coverage as distinct data-scaling axes, limited to their tested regime.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses spatially supervised contrastive pretraining of image ViTs and evaluates frozen representations with cytoarchitectonic linear-probe macro-F1; it does not use language models or held-out next-token cross-entropy.
record.method_sensitivity: The observed downstream outcome depends on how the fixed sample budget is allocated: increasing source count alone has no detectable effect, while adding subjects together with available samples improves scores. Compute gains diminish at the second doubling. Coverage and subject-gating conditions also alter outcomes, though these are not direct tests of the claim versions.

fits_no_version.finding: At a fixed ~450k unique samples, spreading data over 1–18 subjects gave no detectable gain: βB=0.0014 [−0.025, 0.028], and no capacity interaction was detected.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: At a fixed sample budget, source diversity adds no downstream benefit beyond the sample count.

fits_no_version.finding: Subjects seen in pretraining scored higher by 0.124 (held-out-section subjects) and 0.148 (transfer subjects) macro-F1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pretraining exposure to a source improves downstream generalization to that source.

fits_no_version.finding: Narrower spatial coverage at a fixed sample count lowered macro-F1 by up to 0.038 at B=13. This effect is confounded with positive-weight changes in the objective.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Domain coverage is a data-scaling axis separate from sample count.

fits_no_version.finding: Larger models reach lower SpatialNCE training loss, and the loss is still falling at 146,400 steps; no fit is reported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training loss of contrastive image encoders falls with capacity and steps.

record.problems: The study uses one optimization seed per configuration and a finite subject pool; the primary evaluation uses three unseen subjects. The fixed-sample subject-count test covers approximately 450 000 unique locations and B = 1–18 only. Some coverage manipulations also change the SpatialNCE objective's positive-weight composition. The downstream measure is linear-probe macro-F1, not held-out pretraining loss.

untested.parts: No held-out pretraining loss and no power-law fit; only the SpatialNCE training-loss trajectory is shown (App. D.4).
No extrapolation from small to large runs.
No shape variation at fixed parameter count; ViT-B/L/H change size.
Image modality is used, but no power-law fit to pretraining loss is reported.
No prediction of downstream score from pretraining loss. The logit-linear scaling form is assumed, not tested for fit or extrapolation. No language-model tasks.
No comparison of fitting choices or exponents for loss laws.

missing.what: Matched-subset capacity contrasts at B=18: 0.300 / 0.311 / 0.316 macro-F1, all below the within-subset MDE.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's limits_scope label on subject count is dropped, because subject count at fixed samples is not a scale axis of V6. V6 is applied here to a non-language, contrastive image setting. Each configuration uses a single seed, and evaluation uses three unseen subjects.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out language-model pretraining loss and power-law behavior in parameters, tokens, or compute.
Whether fits from small runs predict losses of much larger runs.
The loss-minimizing parameter/token allocation at fixed compute and its trend with compute.
Architecture comparisons at fixed parameter count; the study compares model capacities, not architecture variations at equal size.

The same power-law form for held-out pretraining loss in other modalities or training regimes. Image models are studied, but the reported scale results use downstream macro-F1 rather than a fitted loss power law.
The paper measures downstream linear-probe macro-F1 for cytoarchitectonic classification in image encoders, not language-model task performance or prediction from pretraining loss.
Whether published exponents or compute-optimal splits vary with fitting choices, or whether the claimed loss curves bend away from a single power law.

rows.subject: ViT-B configurations

rows.value: All seven configurations improved by 0.008 to 0.034 macro-F1

relationships.condition: Image ViTs with SpatialNCE pretraining: unique samples, optimization steps and capacity (pooled), on linear-probe macro-F1
relationships.reason: Positive per-doubling coefficients for samples and compute (R1, R2) and pooled capacity terms above zero (R3, R4). Macro-F1 rose 0.214→0.300 with 450k→9.8M samples (R10, R12, R13), and all doubled-compute runs improved (R11).
relationships.display_finding: Sample and compute doubling coefficients and pooled capacity effects were positive, macro-F1 rose from 0.214 to 0.300 with 450k→9.8M samples, and every doubled-compute run improved.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.reason: R11 reports improvement for all seven configurations. V6 does not require constant gains per doubling, so diminishing gains do not establish a limitation. Moreover, the reported gains are on macro-F1, whereas the fitted coefficient is on logit macro-F1; unequal raw-score gains do not directly falsify that fitted form.

relationships.reason: From the text (no row): ViT-B 0.300, ViT-L 0.311, ViT-H 0.316. None reaches the within-subset MDE despite about 7x more parameters; only pooled terms show a capacity effect.
relationships.display_finding: ViT-B, ViT-L and ViT-H scored 0.300, 0.311 and 0.316 despite roughly 7× parameter growth, with no within-subset difference reaching the minimum detectable effect and a capacity effect emerging only after pooling.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.reason: Section 4.3 reports only small matched-subset increases, 0.300 to 0.311 to 0.316, below the applicable MDE. This qualifies detectable capacity benefits in this condition; the contrasts remain unresolved rather than demonstrating an absent or reversed effect.
